A provincial Russian petrol station at dusk in winter, photographed from the roadside at standing eye level. A queue of mud-spattered cars, vans and military trucks stretches away down the road until it disappears into haze. Hand-written cardboard notices are taped to the pumps, two of the nozzles are bagged off, and stacked empty jerry cans lean against the kiosk wall. In the upper right, framed from the chest up, a Russian man in his fifties in a worn quilted coat stands beside his open driver's door looking down the line, heavy lowered eyelids, outer eyebrows sagging, lips pressed shut, one hand resting on the roof of the car. Style: candid documentary photograph of a real place, not an advertisement, not CGI, not a composite.
